title: Unknown top-level manifest field is rejected by the strict client parser
question_or_target: Does the strict parser reject a plugin manifest carrying an unknown top-level field, with an error naming the field? PASS requires rejection under the STRICTEST supported client, and the authoring toolchain must never emit such a field.

evidence.claim: Independent reviewer verified the artifact at command-center/receipts/TST-0179.json exists on disk (23267 LF-normalized bytes), parses as JSON, carried the builder terminal state=BLOCKED with failure.classification=[reviewer-absent] and reviewer=null (no self-certification) at review time, and its report.kind=parser_report matches the catalog output_schema pin.

probes.raw_output: parsed OK; builder state=BLOCKED; classification=[reviewer-absent]; reviewer=null

evidence.claim: Independent reviewer re-ran both named probes live for 3 rounds each under the ambient environment; all exited 0 with the unit SUCCESS sentinel (probe1_unknown_field.py=3/3 rounds rc0; probe2_emitter_subset.py=3/3 rounds rc0); live sentinels match the builder-recorded raw_output lines (consistent=True).
